descriptions:
A day in the green heart of the Rif mountains: you drive about 45 minutes from Chefchaouen to Akchour, walk along the river with a local guide to the waterfalls or God's Bridge, have lunch by the water and return to the blue city in the late afternoon.

Akchour sits inside Talassemtane National Park, a protected area of limestone gorges, oak and cedar forest and clear mountain rivers. From the dam, the trail follows the Farda river upstream, crossing small wooden bridges and stepping stones, past turquoise pools and little cafés built beside the water. The first waterfall is about an hour away on an easy path, perfect for families. From there you can continue up the gorge to the great waterfall, a longer and rockier walk, or take the other trail to God's Bridge (Pont de Dieu), a natural rock arch about 25 metres high that spans the river. Your guide helps you choose according to your fitness and the season.

After the walk, have lunch at a riverside café, where tagines and grilled meat are cooked over charcoal, and cool down in one of the pools if the weather allows. In the afternoon you walk back the same way and your driver takes you back to Chefchaouen around 17:00.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up at your riad.
09:45 – Akchour dam: start walking with your guide.
10:45 – First waterfall (easy route).
11:00 – Continue to the great waterfall (about 1.5–2 hours more) or take the trail to God's Bridge (about 1.5 hours one way).
13:30 – Lunch at a riverside café (not included).
14:30 – Swim and relax.
16:00 – Walk back to the car.
17:00 – Drop-off in Chefchaouen.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Paths are rocky and sometimes cross the river; wear shoes with good grip that can get wet.
• In summer, the valley is busy at weekends; weekdays are quieter.
• Bring water, sun cream and a hat; there is shade along much of the trail.

INCLUDED: transfer from and to Chefchaouen, local guide.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: after heavy rain, the river rises; your guide chooses safe paths.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Tagines and grilled meat at riverside cafés, fresh orange juice.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The turquoise pools.
• God's Bridge from below and from above.

ACCESSIBILITY
Not suitable for wheelchairs; the first section is the easiest.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the natural beauty of the Rif.

faq.question: How hard is the hike?
faq.answer: You choose. The walk to the first waterfall is easy, about one hour each way on a clear path. God's Bridge and the great waterfall are moderate to challenging, with rocky sections, some climbing and river crossings, about 4 to 5 hours of walking in total. Your guide adapts the route to your group.

faq.question: Can I swim?
faq.answer: Yes, in summer, in the natural pools below the waterfalls. The water is fresh mountain water and cold even in July, which is very welcome after the walk. Ask your guide which pools are safe on the day.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. You eat at one of the small cafés by the river, which serve tagines, grilled meat, salads and fresh juice at simple, fair prices. Bring some cash in dirhams, as cards aren't accepted.

faq.question: Is it a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guide are for your group only, so the pace, the route and the length of the walk follow what you want.

faq.question: Can children join?
faq.answer: Yes, on the easy route to the first waterfall, which most children enjoy, especially the pools and the river crossings. The longer trails are better for older children used to walking.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Akchour?
faq.answer: May to October is best for swimming and dry paths. Spring has the strongest waterfalls and the greenest valley. In winter and after heavy rain the river can be high and some trails may close; your guide chooses a safe route.

faq.question: What is God's Bridge?
faq.answer: God's Bridge (Pont de Dieu) is a natural rock arch about 25 metres high, carved by the river through the limestone. The trail lets you see it from below, from the riverbed, and from above, where a path crosses the top of the arch. It's one of the most striking natural sights in northern Morocco.

faq.question: Where is Akchour, and how long is the drive?
faq.answer: Akchour is in Talassemtane National Park, about 30 km east of Chefchaouen, around 45 minutes by road. Pick-up and drop-off are at your riad or hotel in Chefchaouen.

faq.question: What should I bring?
faq.answer: Shoes with good grip that can get wet (or sandals with straps), swimwear and a small towel, a hat, sun cream, water and some cash for lunch and drinks. A light jacket is useful in spring and autumn, when mornings in the mountains are cool.

faq.question: Do I need a guide in Akchour?
faq.answer: The main trail is easy to follow, but a local guide knows which paths are safe after rain, where to cross the river and how long each route really takes. Guides also share the history and nature of Talassemtane National Park and help you avoid the busiest spots.

faq.question: Can I combine this hike with travelling on from Chefchaouen?
faq.answer: Yes. As the tour is private, we can pick you up with your luggage in the morning and drop you in Fes, Tangier or Tetouan after the hike instead of returning to Chefchaouen. Ask us when booking, and we'll adjust the timing and price.

faq.question: Is it suitable for older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes, on the easy route. The path to the first waterfall is mostly flat, with a few uneven sections, and there are cafés to rest along the way. The longer trails involve rocky climbs and are better for people with good fitness.

faq.question: Is there a phone signal and are there toilets?
faq.answer: The phone signal is weak or absent in much of the gorge, so your guide stays with you and knows the area. The riverside cafés have simple toilets, which you can use when you buy a drink or a meal.
